feed.title: Mateusz Pachulski – Learning
feed.subtitle: Short cards on things I learned: the gap, what made it click, and how I checked it.

entry.title: A BLE UUID says what kind of data, not which device
entry.summary: In BLE, a UUID names a kind of service or characteristic and is the same on every device of that model. The device address is what tells two devices apart.

entry.title: A green build doesn't prove implementation() is right
entry.summary: If a module's public API uses a type from another module, that dependency has to be api(). The modules that use it today can hide the mistake.

entry.title: testFixtures share fakes between modules without shipping them
entry.summary: The java-test-fixtures plugin gives a module a third source set for fakes and builders. Other modules' tests can use it, and it stays out of the production jar.

entry.title: Objects don't run on threads. Whoever calls them does.
entry.summary: An object doesn't belong to a thread. Its method runs on whichever thread calls it, which is why "run this on the main thread" means putting a message in the main thread's queue.

entry.title: Swift loses the type of a Kotlin Flow, because Flow is an interface
entry.summary: Kotlin/Native talks to Swift through an Objective-C header, and Objective-C only puts generics on classes. Flow is an interface, so its element type doesn't survive the trip.
